assumptions.module_com: Balanced at the central grasp; point payload for kinematics/torque.
assumptions.base_location: Stationary shoulder 10 cm beside the cube near face, level with its center.
assumptions.orientation_sampling: 24 cardinal direction/roll rotations, 64 seeded random rotations, and 2 inward-facing rotations at each position.
assumptions.note: Concept validation only. No CAD, Isaac Sim dynamics, geometry collision, structural or physical lifting tests.

concepts.name: 350 + 350 mm spherical-wrist arm
concepts.subtitle: Fixed arm base beside the cube
concepts.description: Base yaw, two parallel pitch joints for position, then three intersecting wrist axes for orientation. Lengths are joint-center spans, not carbon-tube cut lengths.
changes: Replace the current distributed roll/bend arrangement with shoulder pitch + elbow pitch.
Place the three wrist axes at one center; keep the existing 167 mm center-to-grasp offset.
Retain the 13 N·m motor limits for this test. No stronger motor is silently assumed.
concepts.verdict: Too short for the full cube

geometry.analytic_claim: All wrist targets are inside radius 1.474664 m; equal links reach radii 0 to 0.700 m with unrestricted ideal joints.

mass_model: Concept-only mass model: six 460 g motors, 460 g gripper, 589 g total brackets/fittings, tubes at 8 g per 150 mm.
Yaw motor plus 80 g hardware are fixed; shoulder/elbow motor centers lie on the corresponding pivot; three wrist axes intersect ideally.
Motor housings and bearings still need a physically realizable wrist design. Mass allocation is a stated concept assumption, not new CAD.
Torque maxima describe the best of four positioning IK branches for the tested poses. They are not certified global maxima or a complete motor sizing specification.
statics.note: Gravity only, including the arm and 2 kg load. Four positioning branches tested per target; axes are ideal, with no joint stops.

limitations: Collisions, finite motor packaging, cable limits, singular motion and assembly paths are not checked.
A spherical wrist changes orientation control; it cannot remove the distance from the fixed base to the far cube corner.
2 kg hardware lifting is not validated. New actuator or counterbalance sizing requires real component masses and motion speeds.

concepts.name: 750 + 750 mm spherical-wrist arm
concepts.subtitle: Fixed arm base beside the cube
concepts.description: Base yaw, two parallel pitch joints for position, then three intersecting wrist axes for orientation. Lengths are joint-center spans, not carbon-tube cut lengths.
changes: Replace the current distributed roll/bend arrangement with shoulder pitch + elbow pitch.
Place the three wrist axes at one center; keep the existing 167 mm center-to-grasp offset.
Retain the 13 N·m motor limits for this test. No stronger motor is silently assumed.
concepts.verdict: Ideal pose geometry passes; current motors fail

geometry.analytic_claim: All wrist targets are inside radius 1.474664 m; equal links reach radii 0 to 1.500 m with unrestricted ideal joints.

mass_model: Concept-only mass model: six 460 g motors, 460 g gripper, 589 g total brackets/fittings, tubes at 8 g per 150 mm.
Yaw motor plus 80 g hardware are fixed; shoulder/elbow motor centers lie on the corresponding pivot; three wrist axes intersect ideally.
Motor housings and bearings still need a physically realizable wrist design. Mass allocation is a stated concept assumption, not new CAD.
Torque maxima describe the best of four positioning IK branches for the tested poses. They are not certified global maxima or a complete motor sizing specification.
statics.note: Gravity only, including the arm and 2 kg load. Four positioning branches tested per target; axes are ideal, with no joint stops.

limitations: Collisions, finite motor packaging, cable limits, singular motion and assembly paths are not checked.
A spherical wrist changes orientation control; it cannot remove the distance from the fixed base to the far cube corner.
2 kg hardware lifting is not validated. New actuator or counterbalance sizing requires real component masses and motion speeds.
concepts.validation: Independent direct FK versus homogeneous-transform FK, and gravity versus negative potential-energy gradient, passed.

concepts.name: 750 + 750 mm arm with extra reduction
concepts.subtitle: Stationary base · proposed shoulder / elbow transmission
concepts.description: Base yaw, two parallel pitch joints for position, then three intersecting wrist axes for orientation. Lengths are joint-center spans, not carbon-tube cut lengths.
changes: Replace the current distributed roll/bend arrangement with shoulder pitch + elbow pitch.
Place the three wrist axes at one center; keep the existing 167 mm center-to-grasp offset.
Add 8:1 output reduction at the shoulder and 4:1 at the elbow, after the existing MG5010 gearbox; wrist motors retain the 13 N·m cap.
Use separate output bearings and a housing sized for the amplified joint torque. Existing PLA holders are not rated for this concept.
concepts.verdict: Ideal reach + conditional static budget pass

geometry.analytic_claim: All wrist targets are inside radius 1.474664 m; equal links reach radii 0 to 1.500 m with unrestricted ideal joints.

mass_model: Concept-only mass model: six 460 g motors, 460 g gripper, 589 g total brackets/fittings, tubes at 8 g per 150 mm.
Yaw motor plus 80 g hardware are fixed; shoulder/elbow motor centers lie on the corresponding pivot; three wrist axes intersect ideally.
Motor housings and bearings still need a physically realizable wrist design. Mass allocation is a stated concept assumption, not new CAD.
Torque maxima describe the best of four positioning IK branches for the tested poses. They are not certified global maxima or a complete motor sizing specification.
Additional transmission mass budgets: 750 g at the shoulder pivot and 500 g at the elbow pivot. Real reducers, bearings and housings must fit these budgets or be recalculated.
Output torque budget = 13 N·m × extra ratio × 0.85. The 0.85 factor is an assumed derating, not measured holding efficiency. No existing 36:1 reduction is multiplied a second time.
statics.note: Gravity only, including the arm and 2 kg load. Four positioning branches tested per target; axes are ideal, with no joint stops. Shoulder / elbow budgets are 88.4 / 44.2 N·m after assumed additional reduction; this is a proposed transmission, not installed hardware. Other joints remain at 13 N·m.

limitations: Passing results are conditional on the new transmission torque and mass budgets. Reducer fit, stiffness, backlash, reflected inertia, output bearings and thermal capability remain unvalidated.
Collisions, finite motor packaging, cable limits, singular motion and assembly paths are not checked.
A spherical wrist changes orientation control; it cannot remove the distance from the fixed base to the far cube corner.
2 kg hardware lifting is not validated. New actuator or counterbalance sizing requires real component masses and motion speeds.
